articles.title: Dining across the divide: ‘He suggested the Clacton byelection was a vanity project. Obviously I disagree’
articles.summary: A Reform politician and an NHS worker had different takes on Nigel Farage, but could they agree on renewable energy or tax policies? Chris, 42, London Occupation Electrical supervisor of the maintenance team at an NHS hospital Continue reading...
articles.content:
A Reform politician and an NHS worker had different takes on Nigel Farage, but could they agree on renewable energy or tax policies?

Occupation Electrical supervisor of the maintenance team at an NHS hospital

Amuse bouche He used to play and referee mid-level community rugby until he got “too old and unfit”

Voting record Conservative for most of his life, then during the pandemic he moved to Reform (in a move his still-Tory husband characterised as “throwing a strop”) because he didn’t agree with lockdown, masks or banning social gatherings of more than six people

Alex I didn’t know what to expect, though part of my job is talking to people with different views. Chris was really friendly.

Chris We got on well. Alex is a really nice, personable guy, and it’s quite hard to question somebody belligerently when they’re so easy to talk to.

Alex I had calamari to start, which was lovely. For the main course, I had fettuccine with lamb ragu and a glass of montepulciano, and for dessert I had my go-to: tiramisu. It was great.

Chris I had the calamari to start, with a minty tartare dip. Then I had a spicy pepperoni pizza, a couple of bottles of beer, and for dessert a really nice lemon tart.

Alex He suggested the Clacton byelection was a vanity project. Obviously I disagree, but it’s a perfectly understandable position. Nigel Farage clearly believes (and I support him) that ultimately his constituents should be the judge – and they gave him a resounding vote of confidence.

Chris If constituents could be the judge, then why would there be another byelection later if he’s found to have breached parliament’s rules? In Clacton, you’d only need about 8,000 people to sign a petition to recall him, which seems likely because almost 10,000 people voted for a man with a bin on his head.

Alex It was a lot easier canvassing for Reform in Clacton than in the local elections earlier this year in London. I got more abuse during that campaign than I had had in 27 years of politics.

Chris I said, imagine how it is now for a canvasser who isn’t a middle-aged, white, Anglo-Saxon male. If you’re a woman, or from an ethnic minority, or if you’ve got a disability, you’re probably going to get a lot more abuse.

Alex Hurtling towards an artificial target of net zero is counterproductive. We’re doing self-inflicted damage to the economy for what’s largely virtue signalling, in my view, because of the 1% of emissions we’re responsible for. Fundamentally, we need to keep the lights on and food on the table. I support more efficient use of our own natural resources, including oil and gas.

Chris I’m in favour of investing in renewable energy; he’s more in favour of bringing energy costs down by extracting more fossil fuels. I said we can do that, but it’s going to make global warming worse. At our NHS hospital, we’re pretty much at maximum electrical capacity, and if we were to install loads of extra air-conditioning units, as people think we should, that would overload our electrical system.

Alex Andy Burnham is not willing to make tough decisions on things like welfare spending. My view would be that we need to look very seriously at things like Pip [personal independence payment] and foreign-born residents being able to claim universal credit.

Chris He was all for shrinking the state a bit, but he didn’t really go into much detail on how he would do that. I think we should try to raise revenue in other ways, such as bringing capital gains tax in line with income tax, going after big corporations because they’re not paying proper tax, and reforming other taxes like VAT and council tax, because I believe those are regressive taxes that hit the people in the lowest income brackets the hardest.

Alex I think that just by having an interest in politics you’ve got more in common with someone else, even if they’re taking a contrary view. Even though we disagreed, we had that shared interest.

Chris We swapped numbers. He was nice, personable and easy to get on with. I imagine he’ll stand as an MP in the next general election, so I’ll probably text him around then and see how he’s doing.

articles.title: Iraola returns to Bournemouth, Premier League buildup and Townsend’s bizarre accident – matchday live
articles.summary: News, discussion and updates before Sunday’s games This weekend’s fixtures | Mail us your thoughts How things stand in the Premier League… At Hill Dickinson Stadium, Thierno Barry fired Everton to a 1-0 win against 10-man Ipswich Town. Continue reading...
articles.content:
“A great menu the fixture computer has generated for us today, looks like it’ll be a long lunch.

“Starting with the Tatties (Celtic) and Neeps (Rangers) up at Celtic Park, can Rangers succeed in dethroning the Hoops where Hearts so miserably failed last time round? McInnes will certainly be hoping to erase that bad memory.

“Plenty of Black Country derbies to enjoy this season with Wolves, West Brom and Brummagem all vying for play-off places or better, so a couple of pints of Banks’s Wolves v Baggies at Molineux should wash that down nicely.

“Then it’s on to the mains: Leeds will be hoping for a big helping of Yorkshire Pudding and lots of gravy as they take on brittle Crystal Palace at Elland Road, with the prospect of spending 3 weeks treating their altitude nosebleed if they win, lording over ancient rivals Man U and Liverpool. Farke will be straight enough to say that they might be nearly a third of the way to safety if so, and he’ll be right. Manage the team, and manage expectation.

“Iraola’s return to the south coast with the aforementioned Reds would normally mean a hearty Scouse (meat and veg stew) but they may find themselves feeding off Dorset apple pie and Blue Vinney crumbs if Bournemouth can reproduce their midweek European form.

“Man City will hope the Etihad will be too much of a hot-pot for the visit of Sunderland, who will have their own plans for hi-jacking things by turning it into a proper Panackelty served with Stottie cake to mop up the points.

“Then it’s all down to west London to see if Fulham’s pragmatic Fish and Chip supper will be too filling to leave room for any fancy Manchester tart, Carrick could do with getting something out of his jam, custard and coconut team, leaving SW10 with any/all the points would be the cherry on top.

“Big things are the target and big things are expected from a Liverpool side containing three £100m-plus forwards. But the learning curve under the new head coach is proving challenging. As it is for the new head coach, too. Big decisions appear unavoidable…”

If you want to keep an eye on the Old Firm derby, be sure to join John Brewin for minute-by-minute updates.

Paris FC extended their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 campaign, beating Liam Rosenior’s old charges Strasbourg 2-1 in a match marred by abusive chants towards the Englishman from visiting fans.

Roberto De Zerbi has acknowledged Tottenham need more from Dominic Solanke after he criticised the physical condition of the forward.

Spurs remain winless in the Premier League after five matches following a dismal second-half display in a 3-2 home loss to Aston Villa on Saturday.

England striker Solanke was hauled off after 66 minutes following another anonymous outing – after a similar showing in a 0-0 draw at Everton earlier this month.

The 29-year-old endured an injury-hit 2025-26 campaign and missed parts of pre-season this summer, but has featured in all seven fixtures this term and only has one goal against Charlton in the Carabao Cup to show for it.

After De Zerbi put his faith in the ex-Bournemouth attacker, the returns so far have been below-par for a player who cost £65million in 2024.

“We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players,” De Zerbi said.

“I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, for sure, but it’s normal for him (after an injury).

“Maybe it’s not good enough the confidence (in) himself in this moment because he’s much better than this Domi Solanke.

“Maybe many, many things can be better than this moment. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.” Press Association

Dave Estherby has messaged in with his thoughts on which manager is the most at risk of being sacked…

“Carrick’s job is harder but De Zerbi has somehow made Tottenham even worse so I’m not sure he’ll be around much longer. The Champions League could be a hindrance for Utd as you mentioned but they could also go and win the thing (spoiler - they won’t).

“Spurs on the other hand are making all the non-league sides pray they get them in the 3rd round of the Cup.

We also have two Championship fixtures to look forward to this afternoon, including a derby as Wolves host West Brom.

Know it's a quiet Sunday but two hours since the Andros Townsend steamroller ATL post and yet no Partridgesque foot like a traction engine comment.

Jose Mourinho said the mental strength of his Real Madrid team gave him confidence heading into the derby clash at Atletico Madrid on Sunday despite ⁠problems with their game.

“In this second spell I’ve understood that it’s getting more and more difficult to hear anything good about Real Madrid. It’s not a problem to be conscious ⁠of our problems. But we ⁠are also conscious of ​the very good things we have in the team,” Mourinho told a press conference on Saturday.

“Alongside the quality it has, this team has a strength which is very significant, ⁠the strength of the group. This gives me confidence.“

The city rivals are separated by two points after six LaLiga matches this season. Reuters

Gary has emailed in about the offside that prevented Thierno Barry from getting a second goal against Ipswich. Brennan Johnson was deemed to be in an offside position and obstructing the view of goalkeeper Christian Walton when Barry’s header was flicked into the far corner of the net.

“You don’t often hear fans applauding decisions against their team, but I thought Tierno Barry’s fine header vs Ipswich was correctly ruled out. Proximity to a goalkeeper surely matters and I don’t see why Pro Ref can’t come out and say that the incident sets a guideline if not quite a precedent.”

Got a minute to spare? Why not try our daily Premier League trivia game, On the ball? Every day a star player past or present is hidden behind nine clues. How many will you need to identify them?

The Guardian's daily football game , On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Here’s a question for you – which of the two managers do you think is most likely to turn it around?

I think Carrick has a tougher job considering Manchester United also have the Champions League to contend with, which you’d expect would impact squad selection.

At the begging of the season there was a poll about who people (supporters, pundits, sports journalists) thought would be the first manager to go. Many put De Zerbi as their Top choice and Carrick second.

Andros Townsend was lucky. Arsenal were absolutely flattened by a steamroller driven by a flock of seagulls yesterday.

“Crystal Palace lack reliable depth or quality in central defence. Maintaining a traditional four-man backline is crucial. It’s imperative that centre-backs Axel Disasi and Honest Ahanor start today. Offensively, Crystal Palace have to be on the front foot, whether attacking from both flanks or through the central midfield. The bottom line is this, Crystal Palace are relegation-bound if they lose today.”

At the Emirates Stadium, Smilla Holmberg rescued a point for Arsenal with a 95th-minute volley against Manchester United.

Chelsea and London City Lionesses climbed the Women’s Super League table with respective victories over Birmingham and Charlton yesterday.

After thumping Manchester United 5-0 last weekend, Chelsea won again as Lexi Potter and Melvine Malard secured a 2-0 victory. Potter found the roof of the net in the eighth minute and in the 71st minute the France star Malard made a quick impact from the bench with her first goal at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea moved up to second and with their goal difference are likely to stay there.

London City lost 2-1 to West Ham last time out but impressed in a 4-1 triumph at promoted Charlton. Isobel Goodwin’s double had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernández restored their advantage before half-time. The German forward Nicole Anyomi made sure the outcome was no longer in doubt with the Lionesses’ fourth after 76 minutes. They sit third, a point behind Chelsea. Press Association

Today also marks one year since the death of Matt Beard, who managed Chelsea, Liverpool and West Ham during his incredible WSL career.

Fans attending every WSL game this weekend have been encouraged to take part in a round of applause during the 13th minute in memory of Beard.

The beloved manager won the WSL title with Liverpool in 2013 and was named Manager of the Year at the end of that season.

Today marks three years since the tragic death of Sheffield United midfielder Maddy Cusack. Tom Garry recently spoke to her sister, Olivia, who is determined to make sure that her legacy lives on.

At Hill Dickinson Stadium, Thierno Barry fired Everton to a 1-0 win against 10-man Ipswich Town.

And at St James’ Park, two early goals from Joe Willock and Lewis Hall helped Newcastle to a 2-1 win over Hull City.

Elsewhere, Coventry earned their first win of the Premier League season thanks to a 55th-minute strike from Jay Dasilva against Nottingham Forest.

Roberto De Zerbi tore into Spurs after their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa. De Zerbi criticised his team’s mentality, but also the physical condition of his players, and said the substitute Mohammed Kudus had disrupted the balance of his team.

He said: “I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance. We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal, we can’t lose balance just because we are losing. I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.”

Speaking of Townsend, his former club, Tottenham, suffered another defeat yesterday, this time at the hands of Aston Villa.

On the bright side, Spurs finally scored a Premier League goal… twice!

Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly ⁠run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up ⁠with his ⁠Prachuap ​teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on ⁠Saturday.

The 35-year-old avoided serious injury and later made a brief appearance ⁠in the match at Pattani. The former ​Tottenham Hotspur player ‌did not see ‌the roller, driven by a ground ‌staff member, coming towards him when he stepped out of the practice area to attempt a pass.

The roller knocked Townsend over and drove up his ‌legs nearly to his waist before the driver jumped off and ​tried to lift it off the player.

Townsend got back up and continued practicing, and came on as a late ⁠substitute while Prachuap cruised to a 3-0 ​victory.

“Turns ​out Stoke away ​wasn’t so bad after all,” ​Townsend later ‌wrote on ​Instagram, ​joking about the English side Stoke City’s reputation as a tough place for visiting teams to play. (Reporting by Chiranjit Ojha in Purulia, ‌India)

Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal were taught a lesson by free-scoring Brighton as their 100% start to the season was abruptly ended on Saturday.

He said: “They deserved to win the game and it’s a big lesson for us. From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear. We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That’s one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game.

“We knew how tough it was going to be and the first thing we had discussed was about the first part. If you don’t get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game. At this level, it’s extremely important to respect and to understand [that] before anything else.”

In the biggest Premier League result of the day, Brighton cruised to a 3-0 win over champions Arsenal at the Amex Stadium thanks to goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés.

Hello, good morning and welcome to another Matchday live! We have four Premier League fixtures to look forward to this afternoon, with Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool all involved.

There is also (another) Old Firm derby taking place as Celtic seek revenge for last weekend’s 3-0 Scottish League Cup defeat to Rangers. And in the Women’s Super League, Ctystal Palace host Tottenham, Aston Villa travel to face Brighton and West Ham take on Everton.

Not only that, we’ll also be reacting to yesterday’s action – including Arsenal’s 3-0 defeat to Brighton.

Isobel Goodwin’s double had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernández restored their advantage before half-time. The German forward Nicole Anyomi made sure the outcome was no longer in doubt with the Lionesses’ fourth after 76 minutes. They sit third, a point behind Chelsea. Press Association
Today also marks one year since the death of Matt Beard, who managed Chelsea, Liverpool and West Ham during his incredible WSL career.
Fans attending every WSL game this weekend have been encouraged to take part in a round of applause during the 13th minute in memory of Beard.
The beloved manager won the WSL title with Liverpool in 2013 and was named Manager of the Year at the end of that season.
Today marks three years since the tragic death of Sheffield United midfielder Maddy Cusack. Tom Garry recently spoke to her sister, Olivia, who is determined to make sure that her legacy lives on.
At Hill Dickinson Stadium, Thierno Barry fired Everton to a 1-0 win against 10-man Ipswich Town.
And at St James’ Park, two early goals from Joe Willock and Lewis Hall helped Newcastle to a 2-1 win over Hull City.
Elsewhere, Coventry earned their first win of the Premier League season thanks to a 55th-minute strike from Jay Dasilva against Nottingham Forest.

Roberto De Zerbi tore into Spurs after their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa. De Zerbi criticised his team’s mentality, but also the physical condition of his players, and said the substitute Mohammed Kudus had disrupted the balance of his team.

He said: “I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance. We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal, we can’t lose balance just because we are losing. I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.”
Speaking of Townsend, his former club, Tottenham, suffered another defeat yesterday, this time at the hands of Aston Villa.
On the bright side, Spurs finally scored a Premier League goal… twice!
Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly ⁠run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up ⁠with his ⁠Prachuap ​teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on ⁠Saturday.

The 35-year-old avoided serious injury and later made a brief appearance ⁠in the match at Pattani. The former ​Tottenham Hotspur player ‌did not see ‌the roller, driven by a ground ‌staff member, coming towards him when he stepped out of the practice area to attempt a pass.
The roller knocked Townsend over and drove up his ‌legs nearly to his waist before the driver jumped off and ​tried to lift it off the player.
Townsend got back up and continued practicing, and came on as a late ⁠substitute while Prachuap cruised to a 3-0 ​victory.

“Turns ​out Stoke away ​wasn’t so bad after all,” ​Townsend later ‌wrote on ​Instagram, ​joking about the English side Stoke City’s reputation as a tough place for visiting teams to play. (Reporting by Chiranjit Ojha in Purulia, ‌India)
Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal were taught a lesson by free-scoring Brighton as their 100% start to the season was abruptly ended on Saturday.

He said: “They deserved to win the game and it’s a big lesson for us. From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear. We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That’s one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game.

“We knew how tough it was going to be and the first thing we had discussed was about the first part. If you don’t get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game. At this level, it’s extremely important to respect and to understand [that] before anything else.”
In the biggest Premier League result of the day, Brighton cruised to a 3-0 win over champions Arsenal at the Amex Stadium thanks to goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés.
Hello, good morning and welcome to another Matchday live! We have four Premier League fixtures to look forward to this afternoon, with Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool all involved.

There is also (another) Old Firm derby taking place as Celtic seek revenge for last weekend’s 3-0 Scottish League Cup defeat to Rangers. And in the Women’s Super League, Ctystal Palace host Tottenham, Aston Villa travel to face Brighton and West Ham take on Everton.
Not only that, we’ll also be reacting to yesterday’s action – including Arsenal’s 3-0 defeat to Brighton.

articles.title: Celtic v Rangers: Scottish Premiership – live
articles.summary: Updates from Old Firm derby, midday kickoff (BST) Get in touch: email John about the game O’Neill has replaced Sam Johnstone with Viljami Sinisalo in Celtic’s goal. This is the explanation, Johnstone having played against Rangers last weel: “I feel that with Sam coming newly into the football club, and not having played for some time, I thought that the two games that he played, it would give him experience of the Old Firm game for a start.” As the Sky pundits suggest, he clearly favours Sinisalo. Continue reading...
articles.content:
8 min: An oasis of brief calm, only for Sinisalo to be chased down when dawdling over a back-pass. Every touch receives a crowd reaction, not bad for so early on a Sunday.

6 min: From the free-kick, Celtic have the ball in the net after Scales flick, Trusty’s volley in, but Scales is offside. So no goal. McInnes got a booking there, by the way. Yes, this is the Old Firm derby alright.

4 min: Fernandez now booked for Rangers , fouling a galloping Duran, who had escaped. VAR has a look, and it is deemed to be not a last-man foul. Derek McInnes and O’Neill are at each other, with one of the Celtic bench given a yellow.

3 min: Did Duran almost escape for Celtic ? It takes a challenge from Fernandez to stop him. He had switched off.

2 min: Rangers have begun the brighter, Raskin playing the ball to Gassama to hit, and it takes a Donovan tackle top rescue Celtic.

1 min: The Celtic fans keep singing YNWA as the game kicks off. The singing turns to boos as Rangers gain possession.

Here comes You’ll Never Walk Alone . Who sang it first? Does it matter? Watch footage from the 1970s and early 1980s and fans of many clubs sing it. It is, though, the song of both Liverpool and Celtic .

This is the 450th meeting of the two teams, and they are on 174 wins each.

Derek McInnes spoke to the BBC: “I know Celtic have made a load of changes. A lot was made of last week, us having won the battle through the middle of the park, they’ve filled the middle of the pitch today. We just need to make sure that we still try and compete in there, that middle ground is important for us to win.”

O’Neill has replaced Sam Johnstone with Viljami Sinisalo in Celtic’s goal. This is the explanation, Johnstone having played against Rangers last weel: “I feel that with Sam coming newly into the football club, and not having played for some time, I thought that the two games that he played, it would give him experience of the Old Firm game for a start.”

Is it actually three at the back? Martin O’Neill, as ever, keeps it mercurial. “We’ve got the options for both - but I’m not sure we’re going to play three or five [at the back]. You’ll find out in about an hour’s time. For years I played three at the back with two wide players. But this is not exactly that system today.”

Derek McInnes also spoke to Sky: “Just because you win the game doesn’t mean it always says you’ve got the tactics right and, equally, when you lose a game, it doesn’t mean it says you’ve got them wrong.

“I think sometimes tactics can get a wee bit overplayed. I do think you normally win games during the individual moments and the performance of players being really high and really strong. We look to do something similar in terms of our approach. We want to make sure the aggression’s there, the confidence is there to play.

“The energy that we displayed last week, these are all the things that are more important than tactics. Hopefully the players go into the game and onto the pitch with that message loud and clear that a big performance is required. You don’t win at Celtic Park unless everybody plays well. We’ve got to try and bring something similar and look for those improvements again.”

Martin O"Neill had the following to say to Sky ahead of the game: “We’re far from rock bottom. We’re still in the lead and if we could win this, we can extend the lead and if we don’t, even by the international break, we’re still going to be in front.

“We’re going to try and put that right if we can. But I know the last time we had an international break was in March time and we played very poorly against Dundee United. So that was, if you can call it a wake-up call or a moment of quiet reflection or whatever the case may be. We turned it round. The players are capable of turning it round.

“It’s a big game, whether it’s played in September or March time. We need to be up for the game. Do we need to win the game? It would be nice to win it, it wouldn’t be great if we lost. That would be three on the trot. Psychologically, it would be a blow. But we need to be up for it.”

Derek McInnes has picked the same starting team from last week’s win at Ibrox. Celtic look to have gone three at the back – the formation that O’Neill had success with first time around at Celtic. Auston Trusty lines up alongside Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales. Kasper Hogh, Haissem Hassan, Oliver Sorensen, and James Forrest are the four players dropped.

Celtic: Sinisalo, Trusty, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Donovan, Baur, McGregor, Tierney, McCowan, Duran, Nygren. Subs: Johnstone, Oxlade-Chamberlain, Hogh, Tounekti, Hassan, Mheuka, Murray, Forrest, Ralston.

Rangers: Pandur, Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice, Kim, Neil, Raskin, Gassama, Naderi, Kelsy. Subs: Kelly, McCrorie, Godfrey, Dragojevic, Devlin, Chukwuani, Curtis, Bouanani, Miovski.

Rangers are out of Europe after losing their playoffs for the Europa League and Conference League, but their fans may well have enjoyed watching the Europa League this week.

Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.

Another week, another Old Firm/Glasgow derby match. Though the next one isn’t scheduled until 3 January. Rangers won last week, and should they win at Parkhead it could blow open the title race. Hearts divide both teams at the moment in the table, and a bad week for Celtic would be completed by losing to their eternal rivals. Derek McInnes was bought time and credibility by beating Celtic in the League Cup while Martin O’Neill was in cantankerous form before and after the Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros. So, plenty to play for, though there’s always plenty to play for.

articles.title: Andros Townsend avoids injury after bizarre pitch roller incident in Thailand
articles.summary: Former England player run over while warming up ‘It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad,’ says winger The former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away “wasn’t so bad after all” following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller. The ex-Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker Townsend currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out before a fixture at Pattani. Continue reading...
articles.content:
The former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away “wasn’t so bad after all” following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller.

The ex-Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker Townsend currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out before a fixture at Pattani.

Townsend was warming up when a member of staff at Pattani appeared to lose control of the pitch roller and it crashed into the 13-cap England international. The left leg of the Prachuap player briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he did feature off the bench late on in the 3-0 win.

Regular ITV pundit Townsend later took to Instagram to make light of the incident, referencing one of his recent posts in which he contrasted a sun-drenched Thai away trip with previous visits to Stoke’s windswept stadium.

Townsend said on his Instagram story: “It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad after all. Swipe to see why.”

Another post described Townsend as ‘The King of Memes in Thai League history’ and he replied “trust me” with four laughing emojis.

articles.title: Luke Littler threatens to boycott Netherlands darts events after booing
articles.summary: ‘If the Dutch stay like this I’m not going,’ says teenager Littler hoping to win all 10 major TV events in a year Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam. The back-to-back world champion faced a hostile environment during Friday’s win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Costorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Nathan Aspinall. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The back-to-back world champion faced a hostile environment during Friday’s win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Costorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Nathan Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

And he is “100 %” prepared to do the same in the Netherlands. “With the Germans, I haven’t been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same,” he told Online Darts .

“If the Dutch stay like this, then I’m not going to do any Euro tours over there. There’s just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I’m getting booed. I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

“The past two nights, I’ve done nothing, I’ve just walked off stage without thanking anybody. There’s no point thanking everyone when they are booing me.”

Despite the bearpit atmosphere, Littler came out on top in a last-leg decider with Aspinall to keep his dream of a clean sweep alive. The 19-year-old is hoping to become the first man to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year, having triumphed in the first five.

Welshman Jonny Clayton awaits in the quarter-final on Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Kimchi tuna and beetroot halloumi: 10 easy, delicious lunch bowls to make for work – as suggested by chefs
articles.summary: A ‘packed lunch revival’ is under way among office workers who want to eat more healthily. From bread salads to rice bowls, food experts offer their ideas Nearly half of office workers are making packed lunches more regularly than they were a year ago, thanks to the rising cost of buying food on the go, according to new research. Does this mean employees will be lunching on soggy sandwiches and ultra-processed snacks? Apparently not. The survey, by online supermarket Ocado, found the “packed lunch revival” was, in part, driven by a rise in the number of people opting for more nutritious “lunch bowl” options, often inspired by ideas shared on social media. With this in mind, we asked food writers and chefs how to make the perfect lunch bowl – something to brighten up your break, and keep you feeling satiated until you clock off. Continue reading...
articles.content:
A ‘packed lunch revival’ is under way among office workers who want to eat more healthily. From bread salads to rice bowls, food experts offer their ideas

N early half of office workers are making packed lunches more regularly than they were a year ago, thanks to the rising cost of buying food on the go, according to new research. Does this mean employees will be lunching on soggy sandwiches and ultra-processed snacks? Apparently not.

The survey, by online supermarket Ocado, found the “packed lunch revival” was, in part, driven by a rise in the number of people opting for more nutritious “lunch bowl” options, often inspired by ideas shared on social media. With this in mind, we asked food writers and chefs how to make the perfect lunch bowl – something to brighten up your break, and keep you feeling satiated until you clock off.

My go-to lunch bowl follows a formula: grains or pulses, something fermented, an easy protein and something fresh and punchy. I often cook a whole packet of quinoa, then freeze it in large ice-cube trays so I can defrost a portion whenever I need it. Otherwise, I’ll use a jar of lentils or beans. Then, I’ll add kraut or kimchi for acidity and crunch, followed by a tin of good-quality fish – I love Ortiz’s tuna in olive oil – or a couple of jammy eggs. A handful of chopped fresh herbs or some pink pickled onions finishes it off. Rachel Khoo , chef, broadcaster and author of several books including The Smallest Restaurant in Paris

I love turning a forgotten courgette into a satisfying Turkish-inspired lunch bowl. Soften an onion in olive oil with tomato salça [a rich paste], then add any leftover peppers and tomatoes you have. Add diced courgette, followed by green lentils and vegetable stock, and simmer until tender. Once cooled, finish with lemon juice, pul biber [aleppo pepper] and olive oil. Spoon over leftover rice, bulgur or grains and top with a dollop of yoghurt and chopped dill or mint. It’s easy, nourishing, filling and full of flavour. Akacan Ağır , head chef at Lokal , London

My favourite lunch bowl is panzanella [a bread salad]. Bread is brilliant here because it absorbs all the dressing and juices, so you can throw it together in the morning and by lunchtime everything has properly melded. It doesn’t have to be the classic tomato version either: I love roasted beetroot, green beans or courgettes, plenty of herbs, then something substantial, such as cheese, eggs or pulses, with a nice sharp dressing. One of my favourite combos is puy lentils, roasted squash, leftover bread and pink pickled onions. It’s colourful, satisfying, travels brilliantly and, crucially, gets better as it sits. Rachel Morgan , owner of Twelve Triangles , Edinburgh

For me, the perfect lunch bowl is full of protein, fibre, good fats and plant variety but, most importantly, it tastes great. I’d start with our miso grain, which includes emmer wheat, pearl barley and marrowfat peas, mixed with lettuce (a combination of red oakleaf, corn salad, cos and sweet gem) for freshness and crunch. Then I add sauerkraut, chicken crackling and shredded carrots with grape mustard for some zest. I dress it with zhoug [a chilli sauce] and tahini for a bit of spiciness, and top with smoked paprika olives and chilli-crusted salmon. Christian West, founder of Pick Your Own , London

You can get lovely sesame paste from Asian supermarkets, which I mix with fish sauce or soy sauce, honey and some bird’s eye chillies. I keep the dressing separate from the noodles until I’m about to eat it, as otherwise it can become claggy. I tend to add edamame beans, beansprouts, tons of finely sliced carrots, cucumber (which I de-seed, so it doesn’t make everything too soggy) and raw courgette. For protein, I’d go for smoked mackerel – or shredded poached chicken, which can be a bit more sociable! Top with crispy shallots or peanuts. Julie Lin , cookbook author and c hef at Tacos Lah , Edinburgh

For me, the perfect lunch bowl is all about getting a good mix of flavours and textures. I’d start with steamed rice, add some roasted or grilled protein – maybe chicken marinated in soy sauce and Shaoxing wine – then pile on seasonal vegetables. I’d finish it with a punchy ginger and spring onion dressing with soy and rice vinegar. You’ve got something comforting, but also fresh and light. I’d suggest keeping the components separate while travelling, then quickly putting it all together when you’re ready to eat. Fai Choi, research and development chef – UK, at Hakkasan

I’m a big believer that the rice needs to taste good on its own, so season it properly rather than treating it as something that’s just there to fill the bowl. My go-to is seasoned rice, avocado, miso mayo, mung beans, pickled ginger and furikake [a Japanese condiment with dried seaweed], then chilli-salt tofu on top. My slightly underrated hero is the pickled ginger. It cuts through all the richer flavours and gives the whole thing a bit of a kick. And don’t be shy with the furikake. Miles Kirby , co-founder and executive head chef at Caravan Restaurants , London and Manchester

For me, feeling satiated after lunch is so important because otherwise I end up having an afternoon crash. I like to do a chickpea riff on coronation chicken with a half yoghurt, half mayo dressing, mixed with finely chopped shallots cooked in mild curry powder. I also add mango chutney or apricot jam for the sweetness. It goes well with sliced grapes and wild rice, and I love to top it with Indian snacks or crispy onions for added indulgence. I mix it all together – it doesn’t look very pretty, but I want every mouthful to have every element of the dish. Amelia Christie-Miller, founder Bold Bean Co

At the start of the week, I’ll usually batch cook some prawns because they’re so versatile and I can create a few dishes out of them without getting bored. For a lunch bowl, I love to pair them with cold soba noodles and a sesame or peanut dressing, topped with something pickled, such as red onion, and something fresh and crunchy, such as cucumber. Finish with crispy chilli oil and a packet of crispy seaweed and you’ve got the best meal deal going – it’s been my go-to for surviving the heat over the summer. Lawrence Burrows , food to go development chef The Sea, The Sea , London

I always start with the base: I like a beetroot puree stirred through quinoa. Then add a pulse, such as butter beans or kidney beans. Keep them soft for something comforting, or roast them until crisp for extra texture. Add your vegetables according to the season: fresh, raw salads work beautifully in warmer months, while autumn is perfect for a tray of roasted vegetables. For extra protein, add something with a bit of character, such as salty halloumi. The joy is that it is completely adaptable. Mix and match with what’s in season, what you enjoy and what you already have in the fridge. Bettina Campolucci Bordi , wellness chef, author and educator

N early half of office workers are making packed lunches more regularly than they were a year ago, thanks to the rising cost of buying food on the go, according to new research. Does this mean employees will be lunching on soggy sandwiches and ultra-processed snacks? Apparently not.

articles.title: This is how we do it: ‘As a Catholic monk, I was celibate. But sex with Orla feels so natural’
articles.summary: Rory left the monastery after feeling lonely; with Orla, herself a Catholic, he’s been making up for lost time • How do you do it? Share the story of your sex life, anonymously We had sex after a week. I remember thinking afterwards wow, everything has changed Continue reading...
articles.content:
Rory left the monastery after feeling lonely; with Orla, herself a Catholic, he’s been making up for lost time

We had sex after a week. I remember thinking afterwards wow, everything has changed

On our first date, last October, I asked Rory how conservative he was and he said: “I have premarital sex, but I’d rather die than eat meat on a Friday.” I’d been single for almost three years and wondered if I’d ever meet someone who understood both sides of me: Catholic but liberal. When we told each other we were bisexual, I felt a huge sense of relief.

He introduced me to his friends straight away and we had sex after a week. I remember lying in bed afterwards and thinking wow, everything has just changed.

I usually struggle to feel present during sex, but I can lose myself with Rory. I orgasmed from oral sex for the first time with him – I’d never felt comfortable enough before. In past relationships, I’d use sex to gain affection and attention or I’d withdraw it to say: please show me you still love me.

Sex was a way to prove I was enough, and so the focus was always on the other person’s pleasure. But with Rory I feel safe, and I don’t use sex as a bargaining chip. If I can’t come, it’s not a big deal.

While training to become a Catholic monk, Rory was celibate for three years, so he’s proven he can go without sex – there’s never any pressure. We have it three or four times a week, sometimes twice on a Saturday morning. That’s my favourite time, when we can take it slow.

In Catholicism, premarital sex is considered a mortal sin, so you’re not supposed to take communion. At mass, when everyone goes up to receive communion and we stay sitting, sometimes I worry about being judged. Rory wonders whether sex will feel less exciting when we’re married.

The sex we have is fairly standard, but emotionally it feels new. Had he continued his training, Rory would have become a priest this year. Knowing how different our lives could have been – that we could so easily never have been together – makes what we have feel even more meaningful.

I converted to Catholicism at 22 and then decided to train to become a monk, joining a monastery just after my 24th birthday. At the monastery, I found celibacy surprisingly easy, despite having a high sex drive. I left because I was lonely. People think the physical side of celibacy is the difficult part, but for me it was the thought that I’d never be able to have a deep emotional connection with a partner. When I left the monastery, I thought I’d never get married; I’m a bisexual ex-monk – too weird.

The first time I saw Orla, she was smoking a cigar. We were at a Catholic society party, and a man was telling her that he didn’t think Catholic women should smoke. She told him to fuck off. She was fun, confident and clearly knew herself, which I found attractive because I’m quite reserved. I liked that she wasn’t a stereotypical good Catholic – there was something different about her and it excited me.

I’ve always struggled talking about my bisexuality with partners and it contributed to my last relationship breaking down. But with Orla, I could be open and vulnerable about it. I feel comfortable with my sexuality for the first time.

The church’s teaching on sexuality is quite strict. I’m attracted to people I shouldn’t be – all the sex I’ve had has been naughty in some way. On the other hand, it feels very natural that Orla and I have sex. It’s a physical expression of our love.

Although the sex we have isn’t very exciting, and sometimes I worry my preferences are too vanilla for Orla, it is passionate and emotional, and that intensity makes it special. We have an ongoing fantasy where Orla is a princess in a tower waiting for me to rescue her. Sex is one of the ways I make her feel safe and reassure her that she’s beautiful – simply telling her rarely works.

articles.title: Ed Davey calls for immediate 10p cut to fuel duty
articles.summary: Sir Ed blamed Donald Trump's war with Iran for damaging the UK economy and pushing fuel prices up.
articles.content:
Sir Ed Davey is calling on the government to immediately cut fuel duty by 10p a litre until Christmas as part of a package of policies aimed at cutting the cost of living.

The Liberal Democrat leader is also urging the government to scrap a permanent increase in fuel duty which is set to take effect in January.

Fuel duty was frozen under the Conservatives in March 2022 and Sir Keir Starmer's government continued the freeze , deciding in May to push back a planned 3p increase in September until the end of this year.

The Lib Dems claim cutting 10p from fuel duty now would mean fuel would drop by 12p per litre at the pump.

Sir Ed claimed drivers should be supported and a temporary three-month fuel duty cut would pay for itself by stimulating the economy.

"Petrol and diesel prices are higher than they've been for a long time because of Trump's mad war with Iran, and people need help now," he said.

The policy would cost about £2bn, he said, adding: "It's a three-month package, a temporary package, but if you look at the extra money the government will get through the energy profits levy, from gas taxes, from VAT and fuel duty, it's self-funding."

In a speech to his party's conference on Tuesday, Sir Ed will make further calls to cut the bus fare cap from £3 to £1, and reduce rail fares by 10%.

He will also call for VAT to be dropped from public charging points for electric vehicles and a review of network costs the Lib Dems have labelled unfair.

Chancellor John Healey is under pressure to raise taxes or cut spending at his Budget next month, amid soaring government borrowing costs.

Asked about Sir Ed's call for a fuel duty cut, Labour Party chair Bridget Phillipson told Laura Kuenssberg: "I'm sure John Healey will be open to any and all suggestions ahead of the budget but actually this is an area where the Labour government has taken action on fuel duty already.

"Whilst I recognise what the Lib Dems have to say on this topic, this is the element of politics about it - they've got their conference, they're making their pitch, good luck to them."

Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

Not just 'Nice Guy Eddie': Lib Dems eager for leader to show radical side at party conference

articles.content:
How will Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options

The first Madrid derby of the season could have a big bearing on the 2026/27 campaign as a whole for Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid with both teams aiming to establish the momentum needed to keep pace with Barcelona at the top of La Liga.

Atléti have won two of their last three home La Liga derbies, but are emerging from a transitional summer with several new signings still bedding into Diego Simeone’s side. Even after recent wins over Real Sociedad and Osasuna, their form is unpredictable.

Real Madrid have won six of their first seven fixtures in all competitions to start the season, but are still searching for the right tactical balance after the return of José Mourinho as manager.

Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s La Liga fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options.

There aren’t many teams on Real Madrid’s level as an attacking force. Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior have combined for 14 goal contributions in La Liga while midfielder Arda Guler has also started the campaign in strong form. Los Blancos have netted 17 goals in six league outings.

As a coherent unit, though, Mourinho’s Real Madrid are suffering many of the same issues that brought down Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa before him. The 15-time European champions still lack a natural No 6 at the base of the midfield and have kept just one clean sheet in six league games.

Atléti are similarly searching for the right balance. Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero are still bedding in, but recent wins suggest Simeone has pointed his team in the right direction again. Sunday’s encounter could be an open affair.

Player to watch: Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid – The French forward remains one of the most exhilarating players to watch in world soccer and has started the season in scintillating form. Mbappé could be the difference-maker who gives Real Madrid the derby bragging rights.

Atléti have won two of their last three home La Liga derbies, but are emerging from a transitional summer with several new signings still bedding into Diego Simeone’s side. Even after recent wins over Real Sociedad and Osasuna, their form is unpredictable.
Real Madrid have won six of their first seven fixtures in all competitions to start the season, but are still searching for the right tactical balance after the return of José Mourinho as manager.
Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s La Liga fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options.

There aren’t many teams on Real Madrid’s level as an attacking force. Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior have combined for 14 goal contributions in La Liga while midfielder Arda Guler has also started the campaign in strong form. Los Blancos have netted 17 goals in six league outings.

As a coherent unit, though, Mourinho’s Real Madrid are suffering many of the same issues that brought down Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa before him. The 15-time European champions still lack a natural No 6 at the base of the midfield and have kept just one clean sheet in six league games.

Atléti are similarly searching for the right balance. Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero are still bedding in, but recent wins suggest Simeone has pointed his team in the right direction again. Sunday’s encounter could be an open affair.

Player to watch: Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid – The French forward remains one of the most exhilarating players to watch in world soccer and has started the season in scintillating form. Mbappé could be the difference-maker who gives Real Madrid the derby bragging rights.

Andoni Iraola will make his first return to Bournemouth since leaving the south-coast club for Liverpool. Four games into the new season, the Reds remain a work in progress.

Liverpool have won just one of their opening four league fixtures while Bournemouth are still searching for their first league victory under new manager Marco Rose. Both teams are struggling to build some early season momentum.

Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s Premier League fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options.

Bournemouth have led in all four Premier League matches they have played this season, but have failed to convert any of those games into three points. The Cherries have showcased their quality in periods of games. Frustration over a lack of points on the board, however, is building.

Similar could be said about Liverpool. Iraola has yet to find the right tactical set-up to make the most of the talent on offer, with the central midfield unit particularly unbalanced. Liverpool don’t have the platform to play the way Iraola wants.

Liverpool’s issues away from home predate Iraola. Indeed, the Anfield outfit have won just four times on the road in the Premier League since last Christmas. However, they have won nine of their previous 12 visits to the Vitality Stadium.

Player to watch: Dominik Szoboszlai, Liverpool – Szoboszlai’s stunning strike against Tottenham Hotspur in the Carabao Cup during the week highlighted the match-winning quality of the Hungarian midfielder who has been Liverpool’s most consistent performer over the last 12 months.

articles.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
articles.summary: Family is determined to ensure her ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death. Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Family is determined to ensure her ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death

O livia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.

Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December, after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England Under-19s international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for Sheffield United’s women’s team.

Olivia says Saturday’s walk, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence the inquest heard. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”

A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off at Sunday’s Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day that goes by where we don’t think about her.

“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.

“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know, her legacy will live on.”

The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing belatedly began on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had previously been set to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.

“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.

“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”

Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during Saturday’s 29-mile walk, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.

This time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. A fundraising page for the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected. Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”

The money is being raised for the the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.

“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”

The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.

“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org , or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

articles.title: Hayen must worry about his Burnley future but fans’ fears are existential

articles.content:
Derby’s stoppage-time equaliser leaves Burnley winless at home since last October and financial problems are mounting

T he greatest moments of Burnley’s history were beamed on to a big screen before kick-off at Turf Moor, accompanied by famous lines of commentary. The final one, the moment promotion was sealed under Scott Parker in April 2025, was soundtracked by: “Burnley are back in the big time.” That feels a long time ago now, with a return to the Premier League a remote prospect.

Burnley appeared to have this game against Derby sewn up, leading through Zeki Amdouni’s first-half header, but a stunning stoppage-time strike from the Rams’ substitute Mohammed Fuseini soured the Turf Moor mood. It means Burnley’s winless home league run could now reach a year, the Clarets last tasting victory at Turf Moor on 18 October. Their last win in any competition in 90 minutes was on 11 February.

The draw left Nicky Hayen, the under-fire head coach, under scrutiny, though the majority of fans will direct their anger towards Alan Pace, the chair, given the financial problems and off-field turmoil that have plagued the club during a disruptive summer.

Hayen vowed to fight for his future and revealed he would talk with Pace, though could give no assurances he will remain in charge for the next game at Watford on 10 October after the extra-long international break. “I can understand the fans are angry after a start like this, it’s not what they want to see from their team or from myself,” he said. “It’s my responsibility. But I’ve always shown resilience and I’m always going to fight. We need this [international] window to change a lot of things.”

In his programme notes before the game, Pace called for fans to “unite and show togetherness”, after they had chanted for his removal during the home defeat by Bristol City a fortnight ago. There was some early encouragement for Hayen’s team as they sought to make early inroads against Derby. Although a lack of thrust in the final third was evident at times, Burnley made the breakthrough via Amdouni’s forehead, the forward peeling around the back post to nod home Lucas Pires’ corner.

Hayen, who was managing Haverfordwest County in the Welsh Premier League four years ago and was not Burnley’s first choice to replace Parker, celebrated. Having been accused of muddled selections in his tenure so far, he had made some brave calls, dropping the club captain, Kyle Walker, and struggling goalkeeper Max Weiss, and recalling Marcus Edwards, who had been jettisoned after featuring in the campaign’s opening two games.

Those decisions were nearly vindicated, right up to the moment Fuseini pounced, leaving Hayen to bear the brunt of more fan criticism. “It is really difficult [to take],” he said. “You saw the reaction of the players after the game, sitting on the ground, disappointed. We wanted to give the fans the win, I wanted this for them, I can accept their frustration. I want to give back to the fans, I feel we can give back a lot. You saw we were close, we wanted to do it just before the international break.”

The break may represent a chance for Hayen, if he remains, to regroup, though for Pace and the board there remain unanswered questions about the £142m of external debt the club owes, as well as the £81m owed by his firm ALK Capital to the club itself after a leveraged buyout in December 2020. Comparisons with the Glazers’ takeover and ownership of Manchester United have been made. James Holroyd’s recent departure, after 15 months as chief executive, feels reflective of the worsening malaise in the boardroom. Holroyd previously worked under the Glazers at United.

Despite two promotions under the current regime (and three relegations) the Clarets’ financial situation has deteriorated, with some fans now harbouring genuine fears of total extinction if debts are not repaid. Parachute payments may help for a time, but Burnley no longer have the cash reserves they boasted in their debt-free era before Pace and ALK when they enjoyed five successive seasons in the Premier League under Sean Dyche. Such stability now feels a world away and problems are spilling on to the pitch. Money has been spent on transfers, with squad turnover high in recent seasons, but there was particular concern when the £20m sale of Zian Flemming was not reinvested in a new striker, with 39-year-old Jamie Vardy hastily arriving on a free transfer after the transfer window had closed.

Hayen ushered on Vardy and loan signing Largie Ramazani to retain a counterattacking threat against Derby late on, as Burnley hung on. But with a slender lead going into stoppage time, their confidence appeared brittle. Goalkeeper Grégoire Coudert had been forced into a couple of late interventions after Ryan Hedges should have equalised for Derby on the hour mark.

Then, just when it seemed Burnley’s winless streak would be broken, the rocket from Fuseini snatched two points away, leaving them bottom of the Championship . “It’s hard to take,” said Hayen. “It’s frustrating.”
